papers.title: SHAPE: Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions A machine learning approach to solar flare forecasting
papers.summary: Two-phase GRU/LSTM pipeline forecasts monthly and next-day GOES X-ray flare classes, achieving MAE 204 flares/yr and TSS 0.351, though persistence is competitive.
papers.tldr: Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions (SHAPE), a two-phase deep-learning pipeline that bypasses sunspot proxies in favour of direct soft X-ray observations from the GOES X-ray Sensor, shows that competitive flare forecasting is achievable with compact architectures that retain in minutes on standard hardware, without sunspot proxy inputs.

papers.title: Recovering Missing Degrees of Freedom in Simulation-Trained Field-Level Generative Models
papers.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures. Expanded manuscript prepared for submission to Phys. Rev. D
papers.summary: Physics-informed latent corrections to a continuous normalizing flow recover missing variability in simulation-trained weak-lensing field-level inference, improving out-of-distribution robustness.

papers.title: Effects of Competing Reactions on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ on Abundance Distributions in Type I X-Ray Bursts
papers.summary: XGBoost and SHAP analyses of Monte Carlo X-ray burst models identify competing proton-capture reactions on 59Cu and 63Ga as main sources of secondary abundance peaks.

papers.title: The Agentic Observer Hackathon: Autonomous Decision-making in Simulated Astronomical Surveys
papers.summary: A hackathon evaluates autonomous survey decision systems from 102 teams; leading systems combine numerical exposure planning with language models for operations and long-term decisions.

papers.title: Learned Surrogates of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Turbulence
papers.summary: UNet, shifted-window transformer, and Fourier neural operator surrogates emulate 3D resistive MHD turbulence, matching simulation statistics and beating prior benchmarks with far fewer parameters.

papers.title: Forecasting the Ambient Solar Wind With a Physics-Informed Learned Inner Boundary: Part I-Differentiable Inverse Reconstruction From Solar Images
papers.summary: Differentiable heliospheric transport maps solar images and magnetograms to solar-wind speed at 21.5 solar radii, outperforming recurrence and linear baselines in cycle-24 validation.

papers.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
papers.summary: Boosted physics-informed neural networks with LightGBM, random forest, XGBoost, and SVR post-correction reduce error and improve generalization for Lane-Emden equations modeling stellar structure.
